practiceQuestions.stem: A 52-year-old has a painless, enlarging deep thigh mass. Before a local excision is arranged, what is the most appropriate educationally safe next step?

options.text: Proceed with a marginal excision to obtain diagnosis.
Arrange specialist sarcoma-team assessment and appropriate imaging before a planned biopsy.
Treat empirically with antibiotics and recheck in a year.
Use normal blood tests to rule out sarcoma.

practiceQuestions.rationale: A suspicious deep/enlarging mass warrants specialist evaluation and coordinated work-up; unplanned excision may compromise definitive planning. The exact patient pathway depends on current local protocols and specialist assessment.

practiceQuestions.stem: For a fictional patient with suspected primary osteosarcoma of a long bone, which statement best reflects pretreatment local imaging/staging principles?

options.text: MRI of the lesion alone, excluding the rest of the bone, is enough.
Obtain local radiographs and MRI covering the entire involved bone; chest evaluation is also part of staging.
Biopsy should be done before any imaging.
A bone scan is always the sole preferred staging test.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The NCI PDQ describes radiographs including the entire affected bone to assess skip lesions, MRI of the primary site to include the entire bone, and chest imaging including CT. Staging choices should be current and individualized.

practiceQuestions.stem: A planned biopsy for a suspicious bone lesion is being discussed. Which principle is most important?

options.text: Biopsy timing and tract should be planned with the definitive sarcoma team after appropriate imaging.
Any clinician may excise the mass first to obtain adequate tissue.
Avoid documenting biopsy path to preserve options.
The biopsy tract does not matter if histology is malignant.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The educational principle is coordinated imaging and biopsy planning with the team expected to manage the tumor; a poorly planned tract may complicate resection. This is a systems/safety concept, not procedural instruction.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which imaging element most directly helps define intramedullary and soft-tissue extent of a primary bone lesion for team planning?

options.text: MRI of the primary site, with coverage adequate for the involved bone.
Plain chest radiograph only.
Bone densitometry.
A single axial slice from CT.

practiceQuestions.rationale: MRI is central to local extent assessment in primary bone tumor work-up; exact protocols depend on tumor site and specialty review.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which pathologic feature is defining for conventional osteosarcoma?

options.text: Tumor cells directly produce malignant osteoid.
Uniform mature cartilage without atypia.
Monoclonal plasma cells are always present.
EWSR1 rearrangement alone defines it.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Osteosarcoma is defined by malignant cells producing osteoid; diagnosis integrates morphology and context, and expert bone pathology review is essential.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which high-level treatment concept is most consistent with current NCI PDQ for Ewing sarcoma?

options.text: Local excision alone is standard because it is a benign process.
Multimodal systemic therapy plus local control with surgery and/or radiotherapy is used, coordinated by the oncology team.
Radiotherapy is never considered.
Treatment is identical to every chondrosarcoma.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The NCI PDQ describes multimodal therapy for Ewing sarcoma, including chemotherapy and local control by surgery and/or radiation; the actual plan is histology/stage/patient specific.

practiceQuestions.stem: A tumor board compares an extremity soft-tissue sarcoma plan with a radical operation. Which general evidence-based statement is best?

options.text: All soft-tissue sarcomas require amputation.
A multidisciplinary team determines treatment; combined-modality therapy is often used, and radiotherapy can reduce local recurrence without proven overall-survival improvement in cited settings.
Chemotherapy is mandatory for every localized low-grade tumor.
Margins and tumor site do not affect planning.

practiceQuestions.rationale: NCI PDQ emphasizes multidisciplinary planning; local treatment choices vary by grade/site and radiotherapy reduces local recurrence but has not been shown to improve overall survival in the described settings.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which best distinguishes an ACGME fellowship milestone from an independent board examination?

options.text: Milestones form a developmental assessment framework for fellows in accredited programs; they are not a standalone board exam.
A Milestone level automatically certifies the learner.
Milestones are a public exam blueprint for all learners.
Every fellowship milestone guarantees board eligibility.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACGME states its Milestones are for fellow assessment within accredited training and not relevant in another context; they do not independently confer certification or eligibility.

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner wants to use images from TCIA’s Soft-tissue-Sarcoma collection in a teaching deck. What is the correct first step?

options.text: Copy images from the web without attribution because they are de-identified.
Review the collection’s CC BY 3.0 license and TCIA use policy, provide the required dataset citation/attribution, and do not re-identify participants.
Assume all TCIA collections are public domain.
Publish patient-level metadata because the dataset is public.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The TCIA collection specifies CC BY 3.0 and required data citation; TCIA prohibits attempts to identify/contact participants. Public access is not a public-domain waiver.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement about orthopaedic oncology board certification is accurate based on current ABOS public information?

options.text: ABOS lists a separate orthopaedic-oncology subspecialty certificate.
ABOS lists Surgery of the Hand and Orthopaedic Sports Medicine subspecialty certificates; its public pages describe primary orthopaedic surgery certification separately.
Fellowship completion alone guarantees ABOS board eligibility.
MSTS recognition is itself ABOS board certification.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABOS lists only Hand and Orthopaedic Sports Medicine subspecialty certificates; ABOS primary certification has separate training, exam and practice requirements. MSTS recognition is a fellowship-program recognition category, not ABOS certification.

title: Orthopaedic Trauma Fellowship
prerequisites: Graduate-level physician learner with completed medical degree and orthopaedic surgery residency or equivalent prior preparation; content is advanced self-study, not a prerequisite pathway.
Baseline trauma assessment, fracture anatomy, orthopaedic imaging, evidence appraisal and professional communication.
MGB’s separate applicant requirements are given above and must be checked on the official programme page; this course does not determine eligibility.
objectives: Reason through major orthopaedic trauma cases using whole-patient, physiology-aware and team-based frameworks.
Describe fracture morphology and imaging uncertainty using consistent terminology.
Compare treatment concepts for adult axial and appendicular trauma, soft tissue injury and reconstruction.
Identify complications, rehabilitation needs, evidence limits, guideline scope and source currency.
Communicate a defensible, patient-centered case summary while recognizing limits of self-study and source rights.

objectives: Describe the orthopaedic trauma surgeon’s role within a multidisciplinary trauma team and identify time-critical threats that precede definitive fracture fixation.

Explain how reassessment, handoffs, documentation, analgesia stewardship and patient/family communication reduce avoidable harm.

Shared decisions and transitions

officialProgrammes.name: Orthopedic Trauma Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official page says one-year programme emphasizing adult musculoskeletal trauma and post-traumatic reconstruction. Fellows work with orthopaedic residents and staff at MGH and BWH. Listed responsibilities include acute trauma, reconstructive trauma care, pelvic/acetabular trauma and osteotomies, small-wire techniques, spine trauma, call, teaching and a clinical/basic-science research presentation. No full public lecture schedule, rotation calendar or exact didactic-hour schedule is disclosed.

programmeSourceScope.type: Official clinical physician fellowship listing, not a residency, combined residency programme, research-only postdoctoral appointment, non-physician supplement, or generic directory category.
programmeSourceScope.institutionalTrack: One MGB fellowship with service at Massachusetts General Hospital and Brigham and Women’s Hospital; preserved under the official MGB title and institutional umbrella. No separate adult/pediatric combined credential is stated.
programmeSourceScope.OTAStatus: The official OTA May 2026 approved fellowship roster lists “Harvard Orthopaedic Trauma” in Boston, two positions. The MGB page does not state ACGME accreditation. OTA roster inclusion is not evidence of ACGME accreditation or a board certificate. No individual MGB ACGME status asserted here.

sourceCaveats: One-year duration and MGH/BWH service are stated by MGB; a complete official didactic syllabus, clinical rotations, case counts and exact training hours are not public on the reviewed page.

OTA May 2026 roster includes Harvard Orthopaedic Trauma in Boston and two positions. It does not label the MGB programme as ACGME-accredited. Do not infer accreditation status from an affiliation or OTA listing.
ABOS and AOBOS sources show no orthopaedic trauma subspecialty board examination/certificate; primary-board credential pathways are distinct.
ACGME 2026 requirements define education for accredited programmes, but do not prove that the MGB programme holds ACGME accreditation.
NICE NG37 latest reviewed 2022; BOAST open-fracture standard last updated 2017. Verify newer clinical guidance, local protocols, and each patient’s context before using clinical recommendations.
The AAOS hip fracture guideline was adopted in 2021 and is limited to older-adult hip fractures.

YouTube duration metadata was checked 2026-10-07; public listing/free-to-view does not guarantee future availability, accessibility in all regions, image reuse rights, or clinical accuracy. Videos are link-only and older content must be cross-checked.

practiceQuestions.stem: Fictional scenario: a severely injured patient with a pelvic-ring fracture is being resuscitated. Which learning response best reflects the orthopaedic trauma fellow’s cognitive role before a definitive fixation plan is selected?

options.text: Choose the definitive construct from the radiograph alone and proceed irrespective of current physiology.
Coordinate with the trauma team, frame immediate threats and physiology, seek needed imaging/exam data, communicate uncertainty, and revisit timing as resuscitation evolves.
Wait for a subspecialty board certificate before participating in the discussion.
Treat the course video as a protocol overriding local trauma pathways.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACGME identifies resuscitation, severely injured patient care, team integration and timing in overall polytrauma care as core knowledge/skills. The MGB fellowship describes trauma-service work but this online course is not clinical training. The scenario is fictional and does not supply treatment advice.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional open long-bone fracture is used in a teaching conference. Which summary most accurately distinguishes a sourced standard from a universal US protocol?

options.text: BOAST (2017) says give IV prophylactic antibiotics as soon as possible, ideally within 1 hour; current NICE and local protocols should also be checked.
Antibiotics should be delayed until the operative wound culture is complete.
The BOAST wording is automatically a national US regulation.
A historical lecture recording substitutes for current institutional policy.

practiceQuestions.rationale: BOAST 2017 states antibiotics as soon as possible, ideally within one hour, but it is a UK professional standard, not a universal US mandate. Clinical decisions require current local protocols and clinician judgment.
practiceQuestions.domain: Open fracture evidence and date checking

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner is asked to classify a pelvic injury from one limited radiograph. Which response best demonstrates safe imaging reasoning?

options.text: Assign a definitive pattern and treatment because every pelvic injury is visible on one view.
Describe what is visible, identify missing views/data, state uncertainty, and use appropriate imaging and clinical context to refine the classification.
Use an unrelated classification system and avoid documenting the view quality.
Copy a faculty slide image into the course to improve visual interpretation.

practiceQuestions.rationale: AO reference and ACGME curriculum support structured assessment and fracture classification; missing or incomplete imaging limits certainty. Source imagery must remain on the lawful host platform.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement accurately describes the MGB Orthopedic Trauma Fellowship from its official programme page?

options.text: A one-year clinical fellowship emphasizing adult musculoskeletal trauma and post-traumatic reconstruction; the stated US/Canada requirements include accredited orthopaedic residency, ABOS board eligibility and Massachusetts licensure eligibility.
A six-year combined residency and trauma board examination.
A research-only position with no clinical service duties.
A guaranteed route to ABOS certification in orthopaedic trauma.

practiceQuestions.rationale: MGB explicitly describes a one-year clinical program across MGH/BWH trauma services. It identifies candidate prerequisites and licensure requirements. Neither fellowship enrollment nor completion guarantees primary board certification.

practiceQuestions.stem: As of the 2026 source check, which ABOS subspecialty certificates are listed by the board?

options.text: Orthopaedic Trauma only.
Surgery of the Hand and Orthopaedic Sports Medicine.
Pelvis and Acetabulum and Spine Trauma.
All ACGME fellowship areas automatically confer a subspecialty certificate.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ABOS lists Hand Surgery and Orthopaedic Sports Medicine certificates, not orthopaedic trauma. ACGME accreditation and board certification are different. AOBOS also lists Hand and Sports Medicine subspecialty examinations, not trauma, as of its current exam calendar.

practiceQuestions.stem: A question bank asks about femoral neck fracture care in a patient aged 70. Which is the best approach to using the AAOS hip-fracture guideline?

options.text: Apply it only within its stated older-adult hip-fracture scope, examine the recommendation and strength, then consider case-specific context and other current guidance.
Assume it covers every adult fracture and makes clinical judgment unnecessary.
Treat an older lecture opinion as higher-level evidence than the current guideline.
Assume one recommendation is mandatory for every patient regardless of circumstances.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The AAOS guideline is scoped to hip fractures in older adults, published December 2021, and says it is not a fixed protocol. It calls for independent clinical judgment in the patient’s circumstances.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional high-energy pilon fracture has marked soft-tissue swelling. What is the most defensible educational conclusion from the public resources?

options.text: Soft tissue and fracture morphology both matter; consider staged planning with appropriate specialist input and verify current NICE/local guidance rather than treating a video’s timing as universal.
All pilon fractures must undergo immediate definitive internal fixation.
A fixed delay applies regardless of limb status or system context.
A free video grants procedural competence.

practiceQuestions.rationale: NICE NG37 covers severe ankle/pilon fractures; current assessment and local policy matter. ACGME requirements address competence but require supervised training; an online video does not confer procedural skill or authorization.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional fracture has not united on expected serial follow-up. Which is the strongest next cognitive framework?

options.text: Consider host, mechanical, biological and infection-related explanations and use appropriate clinical/radiographic evaluation before discussing a reconstruction plan.
Assume infection is excluded if there is no fever.
Label every delayed union a nonunion without reviewing the clinical course.
Select a procedure based only on the oldest video in the playlist.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACGME requires knowledge of complications and treatment of nonunion/malunion; the AO reference and open review provide structured learning. A vignette cannot establish a real diagnosis or plan.

practiceQuestions.stem: A trauma fellow cites a 2019 webinar for a current management statement. What is the best evidence habit?

options.text: Treat the talk as context, identify its date and claim, and verify dynamic clinical recommendations against current guidance and local policy.
Assume public video content remains current forever.
Prefer the longest video regardless of date or source.
Rewrite the presenter’s statement as an official ACGME requirement.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Clinical recommendations evolve. The curriculum distinguishes ACGME educational requirements, board status and clinical guidelines; older recordings are not guidelines and do not establish current practice.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement about use of linked clinical teaching videos and images is correct?

options.text: Public viewing means images may be downloaded and rehosted freely.
Link to the original source, respect its terms, do not copy patient records or images, and verify de-identification/rights before any use.
A made-up vignette is an authentic patient record.
YouTube availability constitutes consent from patients depicted.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Free-to-view does not equal permission to reproduce, rehost or repurpose clinical imagery. Source pages do not independently verify every case’s image provenance/deidentification, so this course links only.

title: Surgical Pathology Fellowship
prerequisites: Advanced learners: completed or ongoing AP or AP/CP residency-level knowledge is assumed; the course is not a prerequisite for, or substitute for, the residency described by programme/board requirements.
Comfort with gross and microscopic morphology, histotechnology, immunohistochemistry, molecular pathology, staging terminology and clinicopathologic communication is expected.
Study only linked, de-identified educational material. Do not use self-study to sign out a specimen, issue an intraoperative diagnosis, direct patient care, or claim procedure competence.
objectives: Use a disciplined specimen-to-report workflow: verify identifiers through authorized service processes, clinical context, specimen type/orientation, gross sampling, microscopic findings, ancillary tests, staging elements and communication.
Construct a differential from pattern, architecture, cytology and tissue context; select ancillary tests to answer a defined question, recognize limitations and avoid indiscriminate panels.
Integrate contemporary tumor classification and site-specific CAP protocols while checking edition, specimen applicability and evolving biomarker guidance.
Explain intraoperative consultation limits, frozen-section artifacts, sampling constraints and the need for direct supervision and prompt clinical communication.
Map topics to ABPath primary AP content specifications without implying a separate surgical-pathology board or validated readiness.
Identify when uncertainty, discordance, rare entities, small biopsies, treatment effects, staging uncertainty or a suspected inherited syndrome require consultation or deferral.

units.title: Scope, specimen workflow, grossing, fixation and quality
objectives: Trace a specimen from requisition through gross examination, processing, signout and addenda.
Identify preanalytic variables and chain-of-communication risks that can alter interpretation.
topics: Specimen identification and clinical question; orientation, inking, sampling maps; fixation and ischemia; tissue conservation; frozen-section triage; quality events and escalation.
boardDomains: AP foundations; laboratory practice; quality and patient safety
units.casePractice: Using an explicitly fictional requisition/specimen prompt, build a gross sampling map and list missing orientation/context questions; no actual specimen data.
units.assessment: Workflow diagram scored for completeness, safety boundaries, tissue stewardship and clear escalation.

units.title: Pattern-based interpretation, differential diagnosis and ancillary-test stewardship
objectives: Describe architecture, cytology, stroma, necrosis, invasion and background as separate observations before interpretation.
Choose a limited immunohistochemical/molecular strategy tied to a differential and explain test limitations.
topics: Pattern-first diagnosis; lineage and differentiation; immunohistochemistry controls; molecular test selection; tumor heterogeneity; discordance and consultation.
units.casePractice: Use linked licensed educational materials to make an observation/differential/ancillary-test table without reproducing images.
units.assessment: Short-answer differential matrix; points for controls, predictive limits and a defensible stop/consult threshold.

units.title: Neoplasia, staging, classification, and synoptic reporting
objectives: Separate diagnostic classification, grade, stage and predictive biomarkers.
Use the current site-specific CAP protocol and document elements that are inapplicable or indeterminate.
topics: WHO/IARC classification updates; tumor extent, margins, nodes; CAP protocol selection; structured reporting; staging edition checks.
units.casePractice: Select the relevant protocol for a fictional resection and mark required versus unknown fields; do not invent data.
units.assessment: Synoptic-template critique against the current CAP protocol, graded for version/date and factual restraint.

units.title: Gastrointestinal mucosal biopsies, polyps and dysplasia
objectives: Distinguish major polyp/precursor patterns and articulate interpretive caveats.
Correlate biopsy sampling with endoscopic site and clinical context without overcalling limited tissue.
Differentiate a GI mucosal lymphoid differential from a diagnosis established by lymphocytes alone; use site and tissue context, an explicit ancillary question, and consultation when unresolved.
topics: Colorectal and upper GI polyps; serrated lesions; IBD-associated dysplasia; precursor lesions; sampling and reporting.
Lymphoid infiltrates and gastrointestinal lymphoma differential: integrate clinical/endoscopic context with morphology; avoid overcalling benign lymphoid tissue or an unsupported neoplasm.
units.casePractice: Review university-linked WebPath examples and label image-level features as educational observations only.
units.assessment: Compare two fictional polyp descriptions and justify a differential and appropriate report language.

units.title: GI and pancreatobiliary neoplasia; biomarker integration
objectives: Construct a location- and morphology-based differential for GI mesenchymal and pancreatic lesions.
State why biomarker results require assay/context-specific interpretation and current guideline checking.
topics: GI mesenchymal differentials; pancreatic core biopsies; HCC adenoma mimics; companion biomarkers; biliary specimens and gross sampling.
boardDomains: AP GI; liver; pancreas; molecular pathology
units.casePractice: Create a fictional core-biopsy differential with adequate-tissue/ancillary-test caveats; no treatment recommendations.
units.assessment: Case-based interpretation memo graded for location, tissue limits, assay selection, source currency and uncertainty.

units.title: Breast pathology: core biopsy, excisions, biomarkers and treatment effect
objectives: Relate specimen type and imaging concordance to the scope and limits of a diagnosis.
Apply current assay guidance and describe residual disease using appropriate reporting framework, not treatment advice.
topics: High-risk lesions; spindle-cell mimics; HER2 and receptor biomarkers; neoadjuvant effects; grossing, margins, response reporting.
Unexpected breast classifications, lobular carcinoma variants/mimics, and primary-versus-metastatic differential; preserve morphology and specimen limits.
units.casePractice: Use only linked educational descriptions: specify radiology-pathology concordance questions, sampling limits and the applicable biomarker protocol.
units.assessment: Structured core-biopsy and post-treatment checklist with scoring for uncertainty, protocol edition and reporting elements.

units.title: Gynecologic pathology and intraoperative consultation
objectives: Explain what a frozen section can and cannot establish under sampling, artifact and time constraints.
Recognize a differential for endometrial and ovarian lesions and communicate uncertainty clearly.
topics: Endometrial carcinoma variants; ovarian primary/metastatic differential; sentinel node assessment concepts; frozen-section artifacts; communication and deferral.
units.casePractice: Write an explicitly fictional intraoperative communication that separates preliminary finding, limitations and deferred questions.
units.assessment: Role-play script rubric: accuracy, concise uncertainty statement, escalation and no unsupported definitive call.

units.title: Genitourinary and renal tumors
objectives: Organize a renal mass differential using morphology and judicious IHC/molecular markers.
Distinguish classification from prognostic significance and avoid overconfident interpretation of emerging entities.
topics: Renal tumor families; mimics; emerging entities; tumor sampling; staging; clinically relevant molecular syndromes.
units.casePractice: Use a public educational case without downloading/rehosting images; create a differential table and identify when an expert review is needed.
units.assessment: Viva-style written defense of selected markers and limitations.

units.title: Head and neck, endocrine and salivary gland surgical pathology
objectives: Integrate site, histology and immunophenotype for salivary-gland and thyroid neoplasms.
Recognize familial or molecular red flags without inferring germline status from a single finding.
topics: Salivary gland histology; mimics; grading; thyroid tumor molecular correlates; specimen and margin reporting.
boardDomains: AP head and neck; endocrine; molecular pathology
units.casePractice: Draft an educational differential for a fictional salivary mass and list questions for pathologist-to-clinician communication.
units.assessment: Morphology/IHC matching task with grade and classification caveats.

units.title: Soft tissue and bone tumors; site-oriented differential
objectives: Use location, age/context, morphology and targeted tests to structure a mesenchymal differential.
Avoid equating a marker or fusion with a diagnosis without the correct morphologic and clinical context.
topics: Spindle-cell lesions; adipocytic lesions; GI stromal differential; sarcoma sampling; ancillary test selection; margin/stage reporting.
boardDomains: AP soft tissue/bone; neoplasia; molecular methods
units.casePractice: Create a fictional site-and-pattern differential and a tissue-conservation plan for confirmatory testing.
units.assessment: Rubric emphasizes category-level differential and test limitations, not diagnostic certainty.

units.title: Frozen section, consultation, discrepancy review and patient-safety communication
objectives: Describe artifact and sampling limitations of frozen material.
Use closed-loop communication, documented uncertainty and escalation in high-stakes signout scenarios.
Recognize that pediatric GI biopsy adequacy and clinical-histologic discrepancy can require specialty consultation; do not generalize adult workflows.
topics: Frozen vs permanent sections; tissue allocation; artifact; time-critical calls; consultations; discrepancy learning and QI.
Pediatric non-neoplastic GI biopsy and frozen-section considerations, including adequacy, ancillary studies, clinical-histologic discordance, and limits of intraoperative material.
units.casePractice: Analyze an invented discordance vignette and construct a no-blame review plan.
units.assessment: Oral handoff checklist assessed for critical data, limitations, acknowledgment and escalation.

units.title: Integrated AP board-domain synthesis and evidence currency
objectives: Crosswalk integrated cases to the current public ABPath AP content specifications.
Build a personal update log for evolving WHO, CAP and assay guidance while distinguishing formative study from exam validation.
topics: AP outline categories; classification updates; quality systems; research appraisal; source hierarchy; explicit course boundaries.
boardDomains: ABPath primary AP content specifications (domain crosswalk; no official weighting asserted)
units.casePractice: Complete an integrated fictional case worksheet and annotate each claim to a current source, marking facts not provided as unknown.
units.assessment: Formative 40-item original question set plus source audit; no cut-score predicts board outcome.

assignment.title: Fictional specimen-to-report evidence portfolio
assignment.instructions: Using only invented case facts and linked, lawfully accessible educational resources, submit six case worksheets (GI biopsy, pancreatic core, breast core, renal mass, gynecologic frozen section, and a quality/discrepancy review). For every case separate observation, differential, test rationale, limitations, classification/staging/reporting field and escalation. Do not copy slide images, patient records or proprietary case text. Mark absent data as unknown.
deliverables: Six 300-500 word case analyses
Two specimen workflow/sampling diagrams
Version-dated source log
Rights-and-privacy attestation
assignment.gradingPlan: Formative rubric: 25% morphologic reasoning; 20% ancillary test stewardship; 20% report/staging accuracy; 20% uncertainty, communication and safety; 15% source currency/licensing. A serious patient-safety boundary error requires remediation but has no certification consequence.

assessment.format: Formative unit checks, written image-free fictional cases, communication scripts and original questions.
assessment.passingClaim: No score is a validated prediction of ABPath performance, patient-care competence, training eligibility or certification.
assessment.integrity: All questions are original study items, not recalled, leaked or proprietary board questions.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional small biopsy shows an atypical neoplasm, but the requisition lacks site and imaging correlation. What is the most defensible next educational reasoning step?

options.text: Infer the most common organ site from the microscopic pattern alone.
Separate observed features from interpretation, seek the missing clinical/specimen context through the supervised workflow, and qualify what the tissue can establish.
Order a broad panel of stains without stating a differential.
Issue a definitive stage based on the biopsy.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Adequate context and sample scope matter; tests should answer a defined question and missing facts remain unknown. This is a fictional study question, not clinical direction.

options.text: It is a current ACGME-accredited surgical pathology board fellowship.

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner is making a blank cancer synoptic template for an invented resection. What is the best way to handle a required element not provided in the case prompt?

options.text: Supply the statistically most likely value.
Copy a value from a similar online case.
Mark it unknown/not provided and consult the current applicable protocol for correct reporting language.
Omit all staging elements.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Structured reporting must not invent facts; protocol applicability and field handling are site/version-specific.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional gynecologic frozen-section scenario has freezing artifact and limited sampling. Which communication is most appropriate for a learner to practice?

options.text: State a definitive diagnosis even when the material cannot support it.
State the provisional finding and limitation, and use supervised communication/deferral when needed.
Avoid communicating any result with the clinical team.
Use a permanent-section grade as if it were certain on frozen tissue.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Frozen material has sampling and artifact constraints; qualified or deferred communication is safer than overstatement. Learners are not authorized to make actual intraoperative calls.

options.text: A single marker result defines tumor type regardless of morphology.

Emerging tumor entities never require molecular correlation.
An online case image alone establishes diagnosis.

objectives: Describe gynecologic and placental specimens using standardized morphology and compartment-based reasoning.

units.casePractice: Fictional case conference using public text case only; no patient record or image copying.
units.assessment: Rubric: evidence integration 30%, uncertainty 25%, completeness 25%, ethics/communication 20%.

units.title: Products of conception and gestational trophoblastic lesions
objectives: Classify common products-of-conception patterns and distinguish molar from non-molar gestations using morphology plus appropriate ancillary tests.
Recognize key differential diagnoses including complete/partial mole, hydropic loss, placental mesenchymal dysplasia and trisomy-associated changes.
Communicate the need for clinical correlation and follow-up by treating clinicians without giving management advice.
topics: Early villous development, p57, genotyping principles, molar lesions, implantation-site pathology, recurrence and diagnostic limits.
boardDomains: Primary AP: products of conception; Pediatric Pathology overlap: placental abnormalities and fetal development.
units.casePractice: Structured fictional case with morphology/IHC result matrix; no proprietary exam content.
units.assessment: Rubric: differential 35%, ancillary-test logic 25%, limitations 20%, clear report 20%.

units.title: Endometrium, cervix, vulva: benign, precursor, and malignant patterns
objectives: Apply morphology-first differential diagnosis to endometrial, cervical and vulvar specimens.
Recognize benign/reactive mimics and precursor lesions; use HPV/p16 or other biomarkers within validated interpretation frameworks.
Report key diagnostic uncertainties and request clinical context/consultation where appropriate.
topics: Endometrial hyperplasia/precursors and carcinoma; cervical squamous/glandular lesions; vulvar inflammatory/neoplastic lesions; cytology-histology correlation.
boardDomains: Primary AP: female reproductive system, histochemistry/IHC/molecular/genomic assays; Pediatric Pathology does not substitute for gyn board pathway.
units.casePractice: Fictional pattern-based differential table for 3 anatomic sites; use WHO/CAP/board material where lawfully accessible.
units.assessment: Rubric: anatomic classification 30%, differential 30%, ancillary-test restraint 20%, report clarity 20%.

units.title: Uterine mesenchymal and biphasic neoplasms
objectives: Distinguish benign smooth muscle lesions from malignant or uncertain uterine mesenchymal neoplasms.
Classify biphasic lesions using morphology and appropriate ancillary/molecular workup.
Recognize syndromic clues while avoiding unsupported germline conclusions.
topics: Leiomyoma variants, leiomyosarcoma, endometrial stromal tumors, adenosarcoma/carcinosarcoma, PEComa, IMT, molecular patterns and mimics.
boardDomains: Primary AP: gynecologic neoplasms and ancillary molecular testing; exam map is overlapping AP content, not a Gyn Path board.
units.casePractice: Fictional consultation exercise with differential, sampling limitations and suggested further review.
units.assessment: Rubric: morphology 35%, differential 25%, ancillary strategy 20%, calibrated language 20%.

units.title: Ovary, adnexa, fallopian tube and precursor lesions
objectives: Use site, architecture, cytology and clinical context to categorize common ovarian and tubal lesions.
Separate primary ovarian from metastatic mimics using an integrated rather than single-feature approach.
Recognize tubal serous precursor lesions and grossing context without treating risk-reducing protocols as universal.
topics: Epithelial ovarian tumors, germ cell/sex cord-stromal lesions, endometriosis-related neoplasia, tubal lesions, SEE-FIM and hereditary risk flags.
boardDomains: Primary AP: female genital tract neoplasms; molecular/genomic pathology overlap.
units.casePractice: Fictional pattern comparison of ovarian tumor pairs; cite actual public cases rather than reproduce digital slides.
units.assessment: Rubric: site/architecture 30%, differential 30%, ancillary/genetic reasoning 20%, uncertainty and communication 20%.

units.title: Ancillary diagnostics, quality, integrated sign-out, and board-style synthesis
objectives: Choose among IHC, special stains, cytogenetic/molecular assays and clinical consultation based on a differential.
Use current standardized terminology and communicate significant findings.
Demonstrate synthesis across gyn, placental and perinatal pathology with transparent uncertainty.
topics: Validated ancillary test limitations; molecular/genomic testing; reporting, quality improvement, consultation; integrated practice questions.
boardDomains: Primary AP board-domain overlap (female reproductive system, placenta/products of conception, ancillary tests and laboratory practice); separate Pediatric Pathology overlap only.
units.casePractice: Submit one integrated fictional report, an evidence map and an error-prevention/QI memo.
units.assessment: Rubric: diagnosis/evidence 30%, ancillary workup 20%, board-domain breadth 20%, communication/QI 20%, source/citation integrity 10%.

assignment.title: Integrated clinicopathologic portfolio (educational, fictional cases only)
deliverables: One gross examination/sample plan for a fictional singleton and one twin placenta; no hands-on specimen work is assigned.
Three structured differential diagnosis worksheets: placental vascular/inflammatory lesion; products-of-conception differential; gynecologic tumor differential.
One concise fictional integrated report and multidisciplinary handoff that distinguishes observation from interpretation.
One source appraisal and QI memo identifying where image rights, access, evidence quality or current practice change the teaching point.
assignment.rubric: 100 points: anatomic orientation and evidence 20; morphology/differential 25; appropriate ancillary test logic 15; clinicopathologic calibration/limitations 20; clear respectful communication 10; citations, privacy and rights compliance 10. Passing threshold for this self-study exercise is 80/100 only as a course self-assessment criterion; it is not board readiness or clinical competence.

assessment.format: 10 original multiple-choice practice questions in JSON, unit quizzes, fictional case synthesis and portfolio assignment.
assessment.scoring: Formative; recommended self-review at ≥80% then re-study missed domains. Not validated, not predictive, not official ABPath examination material.
assessment.practiceQuestionsNotice: Questions are original educational items, not copied or leaked board questions. Fictional cases do not represent real patients.

studyHours.plan: 144 planned independent study hours over 12 weeks (12 hours/week: 3 hours public video, 5 hours reading/notes, 3 hours case reasoning, 1 hour assessment/reflection). This is a transparent study plan, not a claimed training duration or clinical experience.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a fictional placenta, histology shows accelerated villous maturation and distal villous hypoplasia in context of growth restriction. Which vascular pattern is most consistent?

options.text: Maternal vascular malperfusion
Fetal vascular malperfusion
Villitis of unknown etiology
Complete hydatidiform mole

practiceQuestions.rationale: The maternal-side perfusion pattern can be associated with accelerated villous maturation and distal villous hypoplasia. This pattern is not, by itself, proof of clinical causation; correlate with history and full examination.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which observation most directly supports fetal vascular malperfusion rather than maternal vascular malperfusion?

options.text: Basal plate decidual arteriopathy
Fetal stem-vessel thrombosis with downstream avascular villi
Diffuse acute subchorionitis alone
Absent p57 in villous cytotrophoblasts

practiceQuestions.rationale: Fetal vessel thrombosis and downstream avascular villi indicate fetal-side vascular obstruction; classify in distribution and clinical context.

practiceQuestions.stem: A placental report identifies acute chorioamnionitis. Which interpretation is safest?

options.text: A specific bacterium is proven by morphology alone
The lesion establishes neonatal sepsis
It is a morphologic inflammatory pattern; organism and neonatal infection require independent clinical/microbiologic evidence
It excludes a maternal inflammatory response

practiceQuestions.rationale: Histology describes patterns and responses; it does not alone identify an organism or establish neonatal infection.

practiceQuestions.stem: A twin placenta is monochorionic diamniotic. What does the shared chorion imply for pathologic examination?

options.text: There can be no vascular connections
Shared placental vascular connections should be considered and documented where demonstrable
The intertwin membrane must contain four layers
Twin territory can be determined precisely from membrane position alone

practiceQuestions.rationale: Monochorionic placentas may have vascular anastomoses; membrane position does not necessarily mark true territorial sharing. Do not infer flow or clinical syndrome from morphology alone.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which is the appropriate description of an SPP Slide Survey online case for a no-cost public curriculum?

options.text: Unrestricted free image license
A public-domain image set
An authentic case resource but participant-access-controlled, so link only if entitled and exclude from unrestricted free-video/image hour counts
Synthetic ground truth

practiceQuestions.rationale: SPP describes case images and discussion for participants; access/participation terms and rights do not permit rehosting.

practiceQuestions.stem: A products-of-conception specimen shows diffuse villous hydrops and absent p57 nuclear staining in villous cytotrophoblast/stroma with appropriate internal control. What diagnostic direction is supported?

options.text: Complete hydatidiform mole, interpreted with morphology and clinical context
Partial mole definitively
Placental mesenchymal dysplasia definitively
No further differential required

practiceQuestions.rationale: Loss of p57 in the relevant villous compartments supports complete mole in the appropriate morphologic context. Difficult cases may require genotyping; no single feature replaces integrated review.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which board has a separate ABPath pediatric pathology certification exam that includes placental and maternal-fetal topics?

options.text: A standalone women’s and perinatal pathology board
ABPath Pediatric Pathology subspecialty certification
ACGME board
CAP case challenge

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABPath lists a separate Pediatric Pathology exam with relevant content overlap. The MGB fellowship page does not establish that fellows become board-eligible for it; eligibility follows ABPath rules.

practiceQuestions.stem: A public free lecture page says 48 min 50 sec and “archived: not available for credit.” How should its duration be treated in this curriculum?

options.text: Exclude because no CE credit is available
Count the publicly accessible recording runtime as a free lecture, but not as CME credit; disclose archived status
Add a 60-minute estimate
Count its slides as an extra video

practiceQuestions.rationale: Credit status is separate from whether a public free recording can be viewed. Count only the observed video runtime, never slide viewing or guessed extensions.

practiceQuestions.stem: A gross placental report raises possible MVM but the clinical history is incomplete. What is the best next reasoning step?

options.text: Diagnose maternal preeclampsia from morphology
State the observed lesions, request/verify relevant gestational and clinical context, and qualify clinicopathologic association
Assign a definite cause of stillbirth
Infer recurrence probability with certainty

practiceQuestions.rationale: Report morphology and relevant context carefully; association does not establish a unique cause or predict an individual future pregnancy.

title: Thoracic Pulmonary Pathology Fellowship
level: Clinical physician fellowship (ACGME accreditation status not verified from the cited public programme page)-aligned independent study
prerequisites: Pathology residency-level knowledge of histology, surgical pathology, cytology, immunohistochemistry and molecular diagnostics; ideally AP residency or equivalent as the programme’s stated entry prerequisite.
Working knowledge of lung anatomy, thoracic imaging vocabulary, specimen handling, infectious differentials and uncertainty communication.
For learner level: pathologists, pathology residents/fellows, and advanced pathology trainees; not a substitute for hands-on supervision or sign-out privileges.
objectives: Recognize pulmonary, airway, pleural and mediastinal morphologic patterns and common diagnostic differentials.
Integrate morphology with clinical history, imaging summaries and appropriately selected ancillary tests; state uncertainty and sampling limits.
Classify common lung neoplasms with morphology-first, tissue-conscious workup and use current reporting protocols within scope.
Apply pattern-based reasoning in ILD, infection, exposure disease, pleural disease, cytology and transplant/vascular contexts.
Use board blueprint content as a study organizer without claiming an official fellowship blueprint, predictive score or exam readiness.
Use authentic public case resources lawfully and preserve source rights, confidentiality and attribution.

units.title: Lung cancer predictive markers, molecular testing, and synoptic reporting
objectives: Explain how specimen adequacy and tumor fraction affect testing choices and why broad multiplex approaches may preserve tissue.
Relate a test result to the question being answered; distinguish diagnostic lineage markers from predictive biomarkers.
Use the applicable CAP resection protocol appropriately and state when its scope excludes biopsy/cytology.
topics: Molecular assay basics, sample selection, tumor fraction, nucleic-acid preservation and test limitations
CAP/IASLC/AMP 2018 baseline and need to check newer local/validated policy; PD-L1 is not a substitute for genomic testing
CAP v5.1.0.0 lung resection synoptic elements; AJCC 9 per protocol; protocol scope exclusions
boardDomains: ABPath AP respiratory: lung FNA—molecular studies AR, IHC/flow AR, adequacy AR; reporting/management; molecular pathology.
casePractice: Use a fictional scant-biopsy case and stage it only from provided fields; draft pending-test comments, never infer therapy eligibility.
units.assessment: One-page tumor-board laboratory plan plus de-identified fictional synoptic stub; rubric: test selection 30%, scope/limitations 25%, tissue conservation 20%, report completeness 25%.

units.title: Granulomatous, infectious, and immune-mediated pulmonary disease
objectives: Classify granulomatous pattern features and build a differential that includes infection, systemic inflammatory disease, exposure and foreign material.
Select special stains/microbiologic correlation thoughtfully and explain why negative stains do not exclude infection.
Recognize pathogen morphology limits and avoid diagnosing organism solely by pattern.
topics: Necrotizing/non-necrotizing granulomas; sarcoid-like reaction and vasculitis mimics
Mycobacteria, fungi, bacteria, viruses; special stains and organism demonstration
Specimen triage for culture/molecular testing; immunosuppressed host and opportunistic infection
boardDomains: ABPath AP respiratory: infections AR, sarcoidosis AR, hypersensitivity pneumonitis AR, granulomas and stains; Lung FNA infections AR.
casePractice: From a fictional necrotizing granuloma description, draft a prioritized differential and appropriate special/microbiology follow-up without overcalling a pathogen.
units.assessment: Ancillary test table and report addendum; rubric: differential 30%, test triage 30%, morphology limits 20%, communication 20%.

units.title: Pleural disease, mesothelioma, and thoracic tumor mimics
objectives: Distinguish pleural-centered lesion patterns from intrapulmonary lesions and use invasion/ancillary testing in a differential.
Recognize mesothelioma and its mimics while avoiding single-marker certainty.
Separate pleural protocol requirements from CAP lung carcinoma resection protocol scope.
topics: Pleural plaques, benign fibrous lesions, solitary fibrous tumor, metastatic carcinoma
Mesothelioma morphology and diagnostic panel concepts
Mediastinal/chest wall, metastatic and unusual thoracic tumors
boardDomains: ABPath AP: pleural plaques C; solitary fibrous tumor C; metastatic carcinoma to pleura C; mesothelioma AR; mediastinum; lung tumors.
casePractice: Use a fictional pleural mass differential table; no images copied. Separate a description of an immunopanel from a definitive diagnosis.
units.assessment: Pleural lesion sign-out and scope annotation; rubric: anatomic localization 25%, morphology 25%, ancillary caveat 25%, protocol selection 15%, report 10%.

units.title: Pleural and pulmonary non-neoplastic disease, transplant and vascular pathology
objectives: Recognize selected transplant-related injury categories and explain why grading/classification is protocol-specific.
Describe pulmonary hypertension and vasculitis patterns without inferring hemodynamics from isolated histology.
Link pathology to clinical context and transplant-team discussion.
topics: Lung allograft pathology concepts and rejection/infection injury overlap
Pulmonary hypertension, vasculitis, hemorrhage and vascular lesions
Chronic pleural inflammatory and exposure-related changes
boardDomains: ABPath AP respiratory: pulmonary hypertension AR; transplant pathology F; vasculitis AR/F; hemorrhage AR.
casePractice: Create a fictional report note that flags pattern overlap and requests appropriate transplant clinical/radiologic correlation.
units.assessment: Pattern differential and escalation memo; rubric: pattern 30%, context 25%, limits 25%, concise handoff 20%.

units.title: Lung cytopathology, FNA/bronchoscopic samples, adequacy, and ancillary allocation
objectives: Identify common respiratory specimen components and adequacy concerns in cytology/small biopsies.
Select a conservative diagnostic label and ancillary workup that preserve material.
Recognize how infection, granulomas, metastasis, and primary lung tumors appear in limited specimens.
topics: Bronchial ciliated/goblet cells, alveolar macrophages, contaminants, lymphocytes
EBUS/FNA, transbronchial biopsy, touch preparation; rapid on-site evaluation concepts
IHC, flow, microbial stains and molecular testing triage
boardDomains: ABPath AP Lung FNA all subdomains: indications, technique, adequacy, infections, benign/reactive disease, malignancy, reporting; respiratory tract.
casePractice: Use only permitted public slide collections; present a verbal interpretation and write a specimen adequacy statement.
units.assessment: Cytology adequacy worksheet; rubric: cellular components 25%, adequacy 25%, diagnostic restraint 20%, allocation 20%, communication 10%.

units.title: Integrative diagnostic conference: clinicoradiologic-pathologic synthesis
objectives: Synthesize gross, histologic, imaging summary, clinical history, and ancillary data into a ranked differential.
State what evidence supports and weakens each candidate and what further information could change the interpretation.
Communicate an actionable report while explicitly preserving uncertainty.
topics: MDD model for ILD; radiology-pathology integration; discordance
Tumor board: small samples, molecular status, stage/report context
Second opinions, consults, quality, reproducibility and diagnostic error
boardDomains: ABPath AP respiratory and lung FNA, integrated with AP core general pathology; no fellowship-specific examination.
casePractice: Two constructed fictional case packets; explicitly label all invented features, no patient record or image reused.
units.assessment: MDD oral case with written report; rubric: evidence synthesis 35%, differential 20%, uncertainty calibration 20%, tests 15%, communication 10%.

units.title: Quality, research literacy, consultation, and capstone unknown-case review
objectives: Evaluate a pulmonary pathology paper for study design, reference standard, cohort limitations and reproducibility.
Use current protocol/guideline versioning and separate evidence from local policy.
Complete an unknown case with reasoned diagnosis, differential, test allocation, report and reflective review.
topics: Quality assurance, diagnostic discrepancy review, consult workflow
Research question, classification changes, image-data governance and reproducibility
Capstone across tumor, ILD and infection; knowledge gaps and continuing update plan
boardDomains: ABPath AP: laboratory management/informatics and cross-cutting molecular/infection; respiratory F; quality and patient-safety content.
casePractice: Use TCGA/TCIA datasets through stated terms for educational research; only the TCIA image dataset is CC BY 3.0, while linked clinical/genomic/histology resources have separate terms.
units.assessment: Capstone portfolio, 10-item self-test and protocol version audit; rubric: diagnostic reasoning 30%, source appraisal 20%, limitations 20%, stewardship/ethics 15%, report clarity 15%.

assignment.title: Thoracic pathology portfolio (independent, educational)
deliverables: One short structured report and differential for each of four linked cases or teaching packets (tumor, ILD, infection, pleura).
One specimen/tissue allocation memo for a fictional small lung biopsy with anticipated ancillary testing.
One MDD case summary that distinguishes morphology, clinical/radiologic inference and unresolved questions.
One 10-question self-check drawn from original questions in the program plus reflective gap log.
assignment.rubric: Evaluate pattern recognition, differential completeness, evidence/ancillary-test logic, sample limitations, calibrated language, protocol scope, citation and lawful data handling. The rubric is educational and not validated for competency or board prediction.
assignment.caseRules: Use only linked host resources under their terms. Do not download or copy patient-level records or images, take screenshots, or redistribute CAP/DigitalScope slides absent documented permission. Fictional constructed cases must be clearly labeled fictional.

assessment.format: Low-stakes retrieval questions, structured unknown-case worksheets, MDD exercise and capstone.
assessment.passingRule: No cut score is represented as validated. Learners may use the self-check for formative review only.
assessment.clinicalCompetenceLimit: No assessment establishes sign-out competence, independent diagnosis, procedural competence, credentialing, board eligibility, examination success or patient-care readiness.

studyHours.planBasis: Illustrative independent-study plan, not measured instruction or clinical training: 13.4525 hours verified public lecture viewing; 22.5 hours reading; 20 hours case/slide practice; 10 hours written assignments/questions; 6.0475 hours review and capstone synthesis. coveredTopics: Normal pulmonary and pleural histology; gross-to-microscopic mapping
Biopsy, wedge, resection, cytology and frozen-section limitations
Radiology-pathology correlation, sampling, artifacts, tissue stewardship
Consult communication and report language

unitMap.text: Diffuse alveolar injury, airspace-filling patterns, and acute lung disease
coveredTopics: DAD/exudative and organizing phases; acute fibrinous/organizing injury as pattern
Organizing pneumonia, hemorrhage, aspiration, edema; treatment effects
Pattern recognition not equivalent to etiology

unitMap.text: Interstitial lung disease: fibrosis, UIP, and multidisciplinary integration
coveredTopics: UIP criteria: patchy dense fibrosis/architectural distortion, subpleural/paraseptal predilection, fibroblast foci, no alternative-feature set
NSIP, organizing, DIP-like, PPFE, unclassifiable/overlap
TBLC vs surgical biopsy sampling limits; MDD; incorporate 2025 terminology update where applicable

unitMap.text: Airways, smoking-related injury, occupational and exposure-associated disease
coveredTopics: Respiratory bronchiolitis, constrictive bronchiolitis, bronchiolocentric ILD
Emphysema and tobacco/vaping-associated injury
Pneumoconiosis and inhaled particles; polarized light; occupational context

unitMap.text: Primary lung epithelial neoplasia: classification and small-biopsy decisions
coveredTopics: Adenocarcinoma spectrum; squamous carcinoma; small-cell and large-cell neuroendocrine patterns
Small biopsy/cytology classification, immunohistochemistry, sample adequacy and tissue stewardship
Mimics, metastases, rare subtypes; intratumoral heterogeneity

unitMap.text: Lung cancer predictive markers, molecular testing, and synoptic reporting
coveredTopics: Molecular assay basics, sample selection, tumor fraction, nucleic-acid preservation and test limitations
CAP/IASLC/AMP 2018 baseline and need to check newer local/validated policy; PD-L1 is not a substitute for genomic testing
CAP v5.1.0.0 lung resection synoptic elements; AJCC 9 per protocol; protocol scope exclusions

unitMap.text: Granulomatous, infectious, and immune-mediated pulmonary disease
coveredTopics: Necrotizing/non-necrotizing granulomas; sarcoid-like reaction and vasculitis mimics
Mycobacteria, fungi, bacteria, viruses; special stains and organism demonstration
Specimen triage for culture/molecular testing; immunosuppressed host and opportunistic infection

coveredTopics: Pleural plaques, benign fibrous lesions, solitary fibrous tumor, metastatic carcinoma
Mesothelioma morphology and diagnostic panel concepts
Mediastinal/chest wall, metastatic and unusual thoracic tumors

unitMap.text: Pleural and pulmonary non-neoplastic disease, transplant and vascular pathology
coveredTopics: Lung allograft pathology concepts and rejection/infection injury overlap
Pulmonary hypertension, vasculitis, hemorrhage and vascular lesions
Chronic pleural inflammatory and exposure-related changes

unitMap.text: Lung cytopathology, FNA/bronchoscopic samples, adequacy, and ancillary allocation
coveredTopics: Bronchial ciliated/goblet cells, alveolar macrophages, contaminants, lymphocytes
EBUS/FNA, transbronchial biopsy, touch preparation; rapid on-site evaluation concepts
IHC, flow, microbial stains and molecular testing triage

unitMap.text: Integrative diagnostic conference: clinicoradiologic-pathologic synthesis
coveredTopics: MDD model for ILD; radiology-pathology integration; discordance
Tumor board: small samples, molecular status, stage/report context
Second opinions, consults, quality, reproducibility and diagnostic error

unitMap.text: Quality, research literacy, consultation, and capstone unknown-case review
coveredTopics: Quality assurance, diagnostic discrepancy review, consult workflow
Research question, classification changes, image-data governance and reproducibility
Capstone across tumor, ILD and infection; knowledge gaps and continuing update plan

topicGaps: Unit 1: specimen handling, low-power normal orientation and adequacy have no complete public specialty lecture sequence; institutional rotation details are not a public didactic syllabus.
Unit 2: acute lung injury has case-video coverage, but DAD timing, overlap and cause-specific differential remain dependent on readings and supervised context.
Unit 3: 2025 interstitial-pneumonia terminology is only partly taught in public video; classification and confidence require current full-source review.
Unit 4: occupational disease attribution, exposure history, particles and polarized-light/EM methods have limited recorded coverage despite an open review.
Units 5–6: tumor case lectures do not constitute a complete current WHO/CAP/molecular testing curriculum; validated local assay menus and small-sample reporting require updates.
Unit 7: infection lecture coverage is helpful but does not provide an exhaustive organism atlas or current local microbiology test-performance guidance.
Unit 8: pleural mesothelioma is covered by the existing V008/V010, but mediastinal/chest-wall tumors, pleural protocol use and uncommon mimics remain thin.
Unit 9: transplant grading, pulmonary vascular disease, vasculitis and chronic pleural disease have little focused public long-form coverage.
Unit 10: lung FNA/EBUS adequacy, preparation methods, flow/IHC allocation, molecular triage and reporting are insufficiently covered by accessible recorded lectures.
Units 11–12: no full open MDD unknown-case curriculum, consult/quality framework or research-data governance series was located; hosted cases and images retain separate access/use terms.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

topicGaps: Unit 1: specimen handling, low-power normal orientation and adequacy have no complete public specialty lecture sequence; institutional rotation details are not a public didactic syllabus.
Unit 2: acute lung injury has case-video coverage, but DAD timing, overlap and cause-specific differential remain dependent on readings and supervised context.
Unit 3: 2025 interstitial-pneumonia terminology is only partly taught in public video; classification and confidence require current full-source review.
Unit 4: occupational disease attribution, exposure history, particles and polarized-light/EM methods have limited recorded coverage despite an open review.
Units 5–6: tumor case lectures do not constitute a complete current WHO/CAP/molecular testing curriculum; validated local assay menus and small-sample reporting require updates.
Unit 7: infection lecture coverage is helpful but does not provide an exhaustive organism atlas or current local microbiology test-performance guidance.
Unit 8: pleural mesothelioma is covered by the existing V008/V010, but mediastinal/chest-wall tumors, pleural protocol use and uncommon mimics remain thin.
Unit 9: transplant grading, pulmonary vascular disease, vasculitis and chronic pleural disease have little focused public long-form coverage.
Unit 10: lung FNA/EBUS adequacy, preparation methods, flow/IHC allocation, molecular triage and reporting are insufficiently covered by accessible recorded lectures.
Units 11–12: no full open MDD unknown-case curriculum, consult/quality framework or research-data governance series was located; hosted cases and images retain separate access/use terms.
medical.sourceReviewNote: Source-cited research and automated checks; not clinician validation or exam-passing prediction.

practiceQuestions.stem: A surgical lung biopsy shows patchy dense fibrosis with architectural distortion, subpleural/paraseptal accentuation and fibroblast foci. No features suggesting an alternative pattern are identified. Which histologic pattern is best supported?

options.text: Usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) pattern
Nonspecific interstitial pneumonia (NSIP) pattern
Organizing pneumonia pattern
Diffuse alveolar damage

practiceQuestions.rationale: The combined features are the guideline-described histopathologic features supporting UIP. Histologic pattern alone does not establish idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis; clinical-radiologic context and multidisciplinary discussion matter.

practiceQuestions.stem: A transbronchial cryobiopsy has patchy fibrosis and fibroblast foci, but subpleural distribution cannot be assessed and sampling is limited. What is the most appropriate interpretive caution?

options.text: Limited sampling can reduce confidence in classifying definite UIP and excluding alternative features
Cryobiopsy proves idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
Any fibroblast focus is diagnostic of UIP
A negative stain excludes all alternative ILD

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ATS/ERS guideline highlights sampling limitations of TBLC, including reduced ability to evaluate subpleural predominance and exclude alternative findings; interpretation belongs in clinical-radiologic-pathologic context.

practiceQuestions.stem: A tiny lung core contains poorly differentiated carcinoma. There is scant viable tumor and molecular testing is anticipated. Which principle best guides next steps?

options.text: Use morphology and a focused, validated ancillary strategy while conserving tissue and documenting limits
Order every available stain before assessing tumor fraction
Report a definitive subtype from one nonspecific marker
Discard the remaining tissue after H&E review

practiceQuestions.rationale: Morphology-first, tissue stewardship and focused ancillary testing are central to small-sample classification. Molecular testing guidance emphasizes adequate samples and efficient panels; assay choice must follow validated local practice.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement correctly describes the September 2025 CAP Lung resection protocol v5.1.0.0?

options.text: It is for specified primary lung carcinoma resection specimens and is not required for biopsy/cytology or mesothelioma
It is a universal protocol for all pleural biopsies
It applies to every metastatic carcinoma resected from lung
It is an ABPath examination blueprint

practiceQuestions.rationale: CAP states its protocol scope covers lung resections for primary NSCLC, small-cell carcinoma and carcinoid; it is not required for biopsy/cytology and directs mesothelioma to another protocol.

practiceQuestions.stem: A lesion shows four patterns including papillary, sclerotic, hemorrhagic and solid areas with two cell populations. Which feature in the CAP teaching case best favors sclerosing pneumocytoma over invasive adenocarcinoma?

options.text: A well-defined pushing border and a dual cell population
TTF-1 positivity alone
Papillary architecture alone
Any intranuclear pseudoinclusion

practiceQuestions.rationale: The CAP case stresses a well-defined pushing border and biphasic cell population; TTF-1 positivity and papillary growth are not alone specific, and overlap/mimics require complete evaluation.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a patient with diffuse granulomatous lung inflammation, which statement about identifying infection in tissue is most defensible?

options.text: Morphology can guide a differential, but pathogen attribution requires appropriate organism evidence and clinicomicrobiologic correlation
Non-necrotizing granulomas prove sarcoidosis
All necrotizing granulomas are tuberculosis
A negative initial stain excludes infection

practiceQuestions.rationale: The infection pathology resource emphasizes interpreting tissue response with pathogen identification; patterns can narrow but do not uniquely identify the etiology. Negative stains do not automatically exclude infection.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which is a fair limitation of the older CAP/IASLC/AMP 2018 molecular testing guidance when building a present-day assay menu?

options.text: It is a dated baseline and should be reconciled with current validated assays, newer recommendations and local policy
It is an exhaustive 2026 list of all biomarkers
It replaces pathologist review
It authorizes therapy based only on a pathology test

practiceQuestions.rationale: The AMP page identifies the guideline release as 2018 and anticipated future updates as the field evolves. The course uses it only as baseline for test selection and tissue conservation, not as a current exhaustive menu or treatment directive.

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner studies lung adenocarcinoma whole-slide images linked through a TCIA/TCGA data resource. What is the proper governance approach?

options.text: Follow the terms of each linked dataset, cite the required collection and do not republish identifiable/patient-level records
Assume every linked image is public domain because the page is public
Remove watermarks and republish for education
Infer clinical management from an image without context

practiceQuestions.rationale: TCIA describes de-identification and the collection lists a CC BY license for the hosted image files, but linked GDC clinical/genomic/histology data have distinct terms and data citation is required. Public viewing does not equal unrestricted redistribution.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement about board certification is accurate for this pulmonary pathology fellowship?

options.text: ABPath lists no separate pulmonary/thoracic pathology subspecialty examination; the AP primary exam is broad and fellowship completion alone does not establish board eligibility
A separate ABPath pulmonary pathology certificate is guaranteed on completion
The pulmonary disease board examination is the thoracic pathology fellowship exam
The course awards an ABPath credential

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABPath’s public subspecialty exam page does not list pulmonary/thoracic pathology; its AP primary exam is a broad examination. Individual eligibility depends on board rules and training; this independent course confers no eligibility or credential.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional ILD conference has a probable UIP histologic pattern but HRCT suggests an alternative diagnosis. What is the best course-level response?

options.text: Communicate the discordance and integrate clinical, radiologic and pathologic evidence at MDD rather than force a definitive histologic etiology
Call IPF solely from histology
Ignore HRCT because tissue is always definitive
Assume all probable UIP cases need surgical biopsy

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ATS/ERS guideline explicitly updates the IPF diagnostic algorithm to integrate MDD and notes that HRCT suggesting an alternative with probable UIP histology is indeterminate for IPF, not a definitive diagnosis.

title: Gastrointestinal Pathology Fellowship
level: Clinical physician fellowship (independent self-study course; not accredited training)-aligned independent study
prerequisites: Advanced pathology learner, usually after medical school and AP residency or equivalent; this course is not physician training or credential.
Comfort with H&E histology, tumor terminology, gross description, immunohistochemistry and basic molecular pathology.
Ability to read current professional guidelines critically, note source version/jurisdiction, and recognize specimen limitations.
objectives: Apply morphology-led differential diagnosis to common mucosal biopsies and resections.
Integrate gross, endoscopic, imaging, medication and clinical context without asserting unsupported etiologies.
Recognize common GI neoplasms, precursor lesions, inflammatory patterns and mimics across luminal GI, appendix, liver and pancreatobiliary organs.
Use current site-specific protocols and AP content specifications with explicit version control.
Explain diagnostic uncertainty, sampling limits, targeted ancillary testing and ethical case-image handling.
Map course content to ABPath AP domains without conflating board blueprints, institutional curriculum or certification eligibility.

assignment.title: Longitudinal GI pathology portfolio
assignment.description: For each unit, create a one-page differential and version/date note, complete linked free videos, and work through public education cases by link only. Capstone is an explicitly fictional specimen/report scenario; no real patient records or copied images.

rubric.morphologyAndDifferential: 0–4: observations, plausible differential, no unsupported leap
rubric.specimenAndContext: 0–4: site, gross/endoscopic context, adequacy and limitations
rubric.sourcesAndVersion: 0–4: authoritative dated guidance with version/jurisdiction/access caveat
rubric.communicationAndSafety: 0–4: clear qualified language; no treatment instruction; rights-respecting use

assignment.suggestedFormativeProgression: 12/16 per assignment; not a validated board-passing threshold.

assessment.format: Unit quizzes; 10 original questions; written portfolio and capstone self-review.
assessment.scoring: Suggested formative review at 80%; not validated, not an official examination, and not predictive of passing.
assessment.rubric: Evidence-based reasoning, differential breadth, source/version control, uncertainty, report clarity and ethical handling.

practiceQuestions.stem: Distal esophageal biopsy, less than 1 cm irregular Z-line, no unequivocal goblet cells. Best statement under the cited U.S. guideline?

options.text: Any columnar mucosa confirms Barrett
Histology alone establishes Barrett
The U.S. definition requires at least 1 cm of tubular-esophageal columnar lining and intestinal metaplasia; correlate with endoscopy
Alcian blue alone is sufficient

practiceQuestions.rationale: The 2022 ACG guideline uses the one-centimeter endoscopic threshold and intestinal metaplasia; histology alone cannot supply missing landmarks. This is a guideline-specific U.S. criterion.

practiceQuestions.stem: Gastric biopsy shows chronic active gastritis but no organism on H&E. Best conclusion?

options.text: H. pylori proven
Pattern can warrant correlation/testing but does not by itself prove a specific infection
All chronic gastritis is autoimmune
No further evaluation can be useful

practiceQuestions.rationale: Inflammatory pattern is not organism-specific; use appropriate testing and context.

practiceQuestions.stem: Limited sample of a pancreatic cyst has bland lining. Best approach?

options.text: Call benign from cytology alone
Integrate morphology, adequacy, site and differential; state sampling limits and use targeted ancillaries
Assume pseudocyst
Substitute imaging for histology

practiceQuestions.rationale: Pancreatic cyst differential depends on sampling and integrated clinicopathologic evidence.

practiceQuestions.stem: Sessile serrated lesion with dysplasia in colon. Best report stance?

options.text: Ignore dysplasia
Classify lesion accurately; follow current protocol and do not infer germline syndrome without evidence
Diagnose Lynch syndrome by morphology alone
Call invasion from crypt distortion alone

practiceQuestions.rationale: Recognize lesion and dysplasia without unsupported hereditary or invasive diagnosis.

practiceQuestions.stem: Villous blunting with intraepithelial lymphocytes. Strongest inference?

options.text: Celiac is pathognomonic
Pattern has a differential including celiac and other immune, infectious, medication and systemic causes
Proves Giardia
Excludes drug injury

practiceQuestions.rationale: Villous injury is a pattern, not a single-cause diagnosis.

practiceQuestions.stem: Colon tumor near serosa, surface intact in examined sections. Approach?

options.text: Automatically pT4
Apply current staging definitions to demonstrated invasion; examine appropriate tissue and qualify unresolved boundary
Use clinical stage for pathology
Call pT3.9 official

practiceQuestions.rationale: Proximity alone does not equal demonstrated surface involvement; use current authoritative definitions.

practiceQuestions.stem: What does official MGB page support?

options.text: Accredited GI residency
One-year MGB clinical fellowship across BWH and MGH, labelled Non-GME
Guaranteed state license
Research-only postdoctoral appointment

practiceQuestions.rationale: The official page identifies one collaborative clinical fellowship, two sites, and Non-GME status; it does not guarantee accreditation or licensure.

This course confers AP eligibility

Practice original board-style clinical reasoning aligned to the ABPath published domains without implying examination prediction.

assignment.title: Integrated consult + laboratory quality portfolio
deliverables: Two specimen/test selection memos; two fictional interpretive consult notes; one AST reasoning worksheet that cites the current locally applicable standard; one assay validation outline; one fictional outbreak communication and quality-measure proposal; a 10-question error log.

rubric.clinical/test reasoning: 25%; question, specimen, method and limits fit the scenario
rubric.evidence and date checking: 20%; cites primary, current sources; identifies version/standard dependencies

assignment.limits: All cases are fictional or linked to public authored educational resources. No wet-lab procedure, patient-specific treatment, clinical authority or competency credential is assessed.

assessment.format: 12 unit retrieval quizzes; weekly case memos; practical-style interpretation worksheets using public cases or fictional text; 10 original summative practice questions; capstone consult/quality portfolio.
assessment.passingStandard: Instructor-created formative thresholds may be used for personal study only. No validated cut score, board prediction, or guarantee of passing.

studyHours.breakdown: 36 planned lecture-production hours are not ready media and are excluded from counted video time. Self-study plan: 12 units x 5 hours (reading, cases and practice) = 60 h; assignments/capstone 24 h; spaced retrieval/error correction 36 h. Learner adjusts with mentor; plan is not actual institutional fellowship time.

topicGaps: Video-hour floor: 34.0241666667 hours remain (36-hour target less 1.9758333333 observed free, unique recording hours). Authored scripts and target minutes are not rendered or counted.
The existing ASM/CDC NGS lecture bank is relevant, but individual Vimeo durations and anonymous playback were not verifiable; the linked records remain uncounted.
The 2026 ABPath blueprint places 49% of questions in bacteria; no new bacteria lecture series with verified runtime was found. The new additions strengthen specimen and blood-culture quality only.

No verified counted external recordings were added for AST/breakpoint interpretation, non-TB mycobacteriology, mycology, virology/serology, parasitology, and broad bacterial identification; use linked current primary readings and supervised laboratory instruction.
The available CDC microscopy/culture/identification modules are interactive eLearning, not recordings; they support learning but do not close the video target.

Quality-system, safety, informatics, reference-laboratory referral and outbreak/infection-prevention competencies remain heavily dependent on local policy and supervised practice; public lecture evidence is incomplete.
Open sources do not provide a complete institutional didactic calendar or fellowship-wide exact teaching hours. MGB sample rotation lengths are clinical experiences, not didactic/video time.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.
