boardNames: American Board of Pathology (ABPath) — Medical Microbiology subspecialty certification
American Board of Medical Microbiology (ABMM) — separate doctoral-level certification; not an ABPath/ABMS subspecialty exam
medical.boardStatus: A separate ABPath Medical Microbiology subspecialty examination exists (one-day, 305 one-best-answer questions, 6 hours 10 minutes as currently described). ABMM is a separate certification for doctoral-level laboratory microbiologists. Eligibility for either board is determined by that board and the applicant pathway; this course confers none. The MGB fellowship is a clinical physician training programme and does not itself state that every track/candidate automatically qualifies for either examination.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: MGB lists eligible/certified AP/CP/combined pathology candidates or internal medicine/pediatrics graduates who complete ACGME-accredited Infectious Diseases fellowship; applicants must be eligible for Massachusetts medical licensure. Confirm current ABPath primary-certification and subspecialty eligibility directly with ABPath. CPEP-to-ABMM eligibility is a separate route; do not infer ABMM eligibility from this MGB programme.

officialProgrammes.institution: Mass General Brigham (Massachusetts General Hospital/Brigham and Women’s Hospital)
officialProgrammes.name: Medical Microbiology Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official MGB page describes a one-year, ACGME-approved clinical physician fellowship; eligibility via pathology or internal medicine/pediatrics plus ACGME Infectious Diseases fellowship; Massachusetts licensure eligibility required. Sample year: bacteriology 12 weeks; AST 12; molecular microbiology/virology 4; mycology/mycobacteriology/parasitology 9; ID consultation 4 weeks if pathology-trained; infection control longitudinal 48 weeks. These are sample rotations, not didactic hours.

medical.programmeSourceScope: This is an independent learning syllabus modeled on public material. MGB is the only clinical physician fellowship in the packet. The separate Johns Hopkins page calls its offering the two-year ASM CPEP Medical and Public Health Laboratory Microbiology Fellowship, open to postdoctoral physicians and scientists; classify as a mixed doctoral-level laboratory career programme, not as an identical ACGME clinical physician fellowship. MGB ID fellowship page separately describes clinical ID training and Medical Microbiology as a differentiated track; do not collapse ID fellowship with Medical Microbiology fellowship. Research-only postdoctoral microbiology appointments are not treated as physician fellowship or board pathway.
sourceCaveats: Official MGB page states ACGME approval and sample rotations; does not publish complete didactics, case counts or lecture durations.
ABPath page supplies exam format/domain list, while the 2026 PDF is used for current blueprint mapping; do not reproduce protected exam items.

ASM page says its linked NGS course totals 50 hours of free training, but Vimeo video runtime/free playback could not be checked anonymously. All candidate entries remain uncounted until each duration and access status is directly verified. Anonymous yt-dlp metadata checks for YouTube candidates were rate-limited/blocked; they were excluded.
A CPEP listing is a generic programme category open to physician and non-physician postdoctoral candidates, not an equivalent ACGME physician fellowship. ABMM and ABPath certifications are distinct.
Public educational case pages may contain real case narratives, but this course makes no claim to independent de-identification verification; link only and do not copy images or records.
Clinical guidelines and AST breakpoints change; verify current method, version and institutional policy before any real-world use.

The 2026 ABPath blueprint places 49% of questions in bacteria; no new bacteria lecture series with verified runtime was found. The new additions strengthen specimen and blood-culture quality only.

No verified counted external recordings were added for AST/breakpoint interpretation, non-TB mycobacteriology, mycology, virology/serology, parasitology, and broad bacterial identification; use linked current primary readings and supervised laboratory instruction.
The available CDC microscopy/culture/identification modules are interactive eLearning, not recordings; they support learning but do not close the video target.

Quality-system, safety, informatics, reference-laboratory referral and outbreak/infection-prevention competencies remain heavily dependent on local policy and supervised practice; public lecture evidence is incomplete.

medical.sourceReviewNote: Source-cited research and automated checks; not clinician validation or exam-passing prediction.

practiceQuestions.stem: A 68-year-old with possible bacteremia has one adult blood-culture bottle collected after difficult phlebotomy; it remains negative. Which interpretation is most defensible?

options.text: A negative result rules out bloodstream infection.
A single negative set may be limited by collection volume and sampling; interpret with clinical context and collection quality.
Repeat all cultures until positive.
The laboratory should report sepsis.

practiceQuestions.rationale: CDC highlights that insufficient volume can yield false negatives; a negative culture is not an absolute exclusion. Do not prescribe a collection action independent of clinical and local policy.

practiceQuestions.stem: A respiratory NAAT detects viral RNA in an appropriately collected specimen. Which statement is best?

options.text: It proves viable virus is present.
It detects nucleic acid; clinical interpretation depends on assay target, specimen, timing and context.
It rules out coinfection.
It establishes severity.

practiceQuestions.rationale: NAAT detects genetic material; detection alone does not establish viable virus, severity, or exclude other causes.

practiceQuestions.stem: A public case describes small colonies with no MacConkey growth and a negative initial Gram stain, later yielding growth from CSF and blood. What is the safest next interpretive step?

options.text: Dismiss as contaminant because initial stain was negative.
Integrate repeat morphology, culture, identification and clinical context; do not infer from a negative smear alone.
Call the diagnosis from colony size only.
Ignore blood culture.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The linked ASM case illustrates why initial microscopy alone can miss organisms and why downstream culture and identification matter. No diagnosis is requested here.

practiceQuestions.stem: A lab reports a categorical susceptibility result without naming the method or interpretive standard version. Which concern is most important?

options.text: No concern; categories are method-independent.
Interpretation depends on method, QC and applicable current breakpoint criteria.
Only organism name is needed.
Older breakpoints are always safer.

practiceQuestions.rationale: AST categories are tied to methods and interpretive criteria; labs must use applicable validated current standards.

practiceQuestions.stem: A positive blood-culture signal occurs in one set after likely collection contamination. What is the best laboratory reasoning?

options.text: Any positive bottle proves bacteremia.
Consider organism, number of positive sets, collection quality and clinical context; communicate uncertainty.
Automatically suppress all skin flora.
Label contamination without review.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Contamination can produce false positives and unnecessary care; interpretation requires context and policy.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best distinguishes a molecular TB resistance assay from phenotypic susceptibility testing?

options.text: They are interchangeable and detect all resistance.
Molecular testing detects selected resistance-associated targets; phenotypic testing measures growth response under specified conditions.
Molecular testing replaces culture universally.
Neither needs controls.

practiceQuestions.rationale: CDC describes molecular detection of drug resistance using sequencing of mutations associated with resistance; limitations and test scope matter.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a fictional cluster, two isolates are genomically close. What additional evidence is needed before concluding direct transmission?

options.text: No additional evidence.
Integrate epidemiologic links, timing, sampling and genomic method limitations; genomic similarity alone does not prove transmission.
Only patient room numbers.
A positive PCR from either patient.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Genomic epidemiology supports investigation but must be interpreted with epidemiologic context and method limits.

practiceQuestions.stem: An assay is moved to a new platform. What is the appropriate laboratory quality principle?

options.text: Assume equivalence if the package insert is similar.
Define intended use and perform documented verification/validation, QC and change control under applicable requirements.
Skip QC during transition.
Change reports without notifying users.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACGME and CLIA quality-system principles support quality, validation, QC and oversight; implementation is governed by local regulatory policies.

practiceQuestions.stem: A CSF multiplex panel is negative, but clinical concern persists. Which response is most defensible?

options.text: The panel excludes all CNS infection.
Interpret panel target coverage and sensitivity with specimen and timing; consider complementary testing with clinical/lab consultation.
Repeat the same test indefinitely.
Report no infection.

practiceQuestions.rationale: All tests have target and performance limits; the ACGME consultation domain includes specimen choice and interpretation.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which description correctly classifies the Johns Hopkins listing on its current page?

options.text: A one-year ACGME clinical physician fellowship identical to MGB.
A two-year ASM CPEP postgraduate medical/public health laboratory microbiology program open to physician and non-physician doctoral-level candidates.
A board examination.
An infectious diseases residency.

practiceQuestions.rationale: JHU describes a two-year CPEP fellowship for scientists and physicians. This is distinct from the MGB one-year ACGME-approved clinical physician fellowship.

title: Thyroid and Parathyroid Surgery Fellowship
prerequisites: Graduate medical education-level knowledge of head and neck anatomy, endocrine physiology, pathology, imaging, perioperative care and evidence appraisal.
The institutional fellowship is for physicians who have completed otolaryngology or general surgery residency; this independent course is not an eligibility substitute.
Learner should be able to read clinical guidelines and distinguish diagnosis, risk stratification, localization and treatment decisions.
objectives: Apply the publicly available ACTPS FPD exam blueprint as a content map, not a claim of exam equivalence.
Describe thyroid/parathyroid anatomy, physiology, disease classification, diagnostic reasoning, imaging concepts, pathology and perioperative risks.
Analyze evidence and multidisciplinary decision pathways for adult and pediatric thyroid disease, primary/secondary hyperparathyroidism and malignancy.
Recognize current guideline dates, the difference between institutional curricula, board blueprints and fellowship descriptions, and the course’s limits.
Use open case reports by link only, preserve image rights, and complete source-annotated fictional exercises.

Coverage remains concentrated in thyroid cancer case webinars, selected Graves and ablation topics, and parathyroid case discussion. PHPT is represented by expert discussions, but systematic recorded teaching remains limited for biochemical differential, localization methods, indication frameworks, primary operations, CKD-related secondary/tertiary disease, and outcomes.
Dedicated verified long-form recordings remain limited or absent for pediatric thyroid/parathyroid disease, postoperative voice/hypocalcemia, rehabilitation, and long-term surveillance.

medical.programmeSourceScope: The packet’s actual specialty is the Mass Eye and Ear/Mass General Brigham one-year clinical physician fellowship. topicGaps: Directly observed public/free recordings total 8.411944 h, 27.588056 h below the 36-hour target. Scripts and target minutes are not rendered media and are excluded.

Coverage remains concentrated in thyroid cancer case webinars, selected Graves and ablation topics, and parathyroid case discussion. No comprehensive verified lecture sequence was found for anatomy/physiology, cytopathology/molecular testing, pediatric disease, broad benign disease, or complete DTC surveillance.

PHPT is represented by expert discussions, but systematic recorded teaching remains limited for biochemical differential, localization methods, indication frameworks, primary operations, CKD-related secondary/tertiary disease, and outcomes.
Dedicated verified long-form recordings remain limited or absent for pediatric thyroid/parathyroid disease, postoperative voice/hypocalcemia, rehabilitation, and long-term surveillance.

The recent AHNS/ATA 2025 DTC webinar is excluded because the direct watch-page fetch did not establish usable full-video access; a related-video card runtime is insufficient. Other candidate items without direct duration/full-playback evidence remain uncounted.
Older webinar content is dated and cannot substitute for current primary guidance, human clinical review, supervised practice, or procedural competence.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional adult has a 1.4-cm solid hypoechoic thyroid nodule with smooth margins, no punctate echogenic foci, no taller-than-wide shape, and no suspicious nodes. Which interpretation best matches the 2015 ATA adult-nodule pattern table?

options.text: High-suspicion pattern
Intermediate-suspicion pattern
Purely cystic benign pattern
Ultrasound proves papillary carcinoma

practiceQuestions.rationale: The described hypoechoic solid nodule lacks the additional high-suspicion features in that table, so it fits intermediate suspicion. The 2015 guideline gave an FNA threshold at 1 cm for that pattern; the course flags that learners must recheck the current ATA index before applying any threshold. Imaging does not establish histology.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient has biochemically confirmed primary hyperparathyroidism and is being considered for surgery. What is the primary role of localization imaging?

options.text: Establish the biochemical diagnosis
Replace calcium/PTH interpretation
Help localize abnormal gland(s) for operative planning after the clinical decision
Exclude all multigland disease with certainty

practiceQuestions.rationale: Localization is used to guide operative planning; it does not diagnose PHPT or exclude multigland disease with certainty. Evaluate the biochemical disorder and clinical context first.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient with a thyroid mass has persistent hoarseness. Which response is most defensible?

options.text: Ignore voice because nodule size is small
Treat the ultrasound category as proof of nerve invasion
Promptly evaluate voice/vocal-fold function and assess possible invasive disease through the supervised team
Assume benign cytology excludes all invasive disease

practiceQuestions.rationale: Voice symptoms affect preoperative assessment. They are not themselves proof of invasion, and an ultrasound category cannot substitute for appropriate examination and team-directed workup.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best describes the ACTPS credential listed by ABS?

options.text: A residency board certificate granted automatically after the MEE fellowship
A Focused Practice Designation developed with ABOHNS, distinct from primary board certification
An ACGME subspecialty board held by all endocrine surgeons
A guarantee of technical competence after passing a course

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABS describes ACTPS as a Focused Practice Designation for a practice area not already recognized by specialty/subspecialty certification; it is not automatic and has eligibility and experience requirements.

practiceQuestions.stem: A thyroid FNA is reported as a follicular neoplasm. Which limitation is central to interpreting this result?

options.text: FNA reliably determines capsular and vascular invasion in every case
Histologic invasion may require examination of the resection specimen; FNA alone may not resolve follicular carcinoma
Molecular testing is mandatory for every nodule
Ultrasound can prove distant metastasis

practiceQuestions.rationale: For follicular-patterned neoplasms, invasion assessment is a histopathologic issue; FNA and molecular classifiers have limitations and should be interpreted in context.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient is diagnosed with medullary thyroid carcinoma. Which additional evaluation is important to consider?

options.text: Only thyroglobulin testing
RET-associated hereditary assessment and associated endocrine tumors, including pheochromocytoma
Assume the disease is always sporadic
Treat the disease as differentiated follicular-cell cancer

practiceQuestions.rationale: MTC arises from C cells and can be hereditary; current disease-specific practice includes RET/genetic evaluation and assessment for associated endocrine tumors. Exact sequencing belongs to the treating team and current guideline.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which source should be consulted for current adult differentiated thyroid cancer guidance as checked 2026-10-07?

options.text: Only the 2015 adult ATA nodule/DTC document
The 2025 ATA adult DTC guideline listed by ATA, while distinguishing the still-listed older nodule guideline
A non-specialist social-media clip
The MEE programme page alone

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ATA official guideline index lists the 2025 adult DTC guideline and separately lists the 2015 adult nodule guideline. They address different scopes; recheck updates.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional ultrasound labels a suspicious neck lesion as an intrathyroidal thyroid cancer, but the patient has high calcium and non-suppressed PTH. Which approach is best?

options.text: Assume ultrasound origin is definitive
Consider a parathyroid lesion/mimic and integrate biochemistry, imaging and expert pathology/radiology review
Skip biochemical review because TI-RADS is definitive
Call it parathyroid carcinoma without pathology

practiceQuestions.rationale: Parathyroid lesions can mimic thyroid malignancy on imaging. Integrate biochemical evidence and image interpretation; the linked open case is an illustration, not a prevalence estimate or diagnostic rule.

practiceQuestions.stem: What statement best describes the MEE programme source as of 2026-10-07?

options.text: A 4-year ACGME residency with an ABOHNS endocrine surgery board
A one-year clinical fellowship publicly described as AHNS-accredited, with supervised OR/clinic work and periodic allied rotations
A research-only postdoctoral appointment
A generic directory category with no programme page

practiceQuestions.rationale: The current MGB/MEE page calls it a one-year clinical fellowship and states AHNS accreditation, supervised cases, clinic/OR and periodic rotations; it is not described as ACGME-accredited.

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner studies adult complex thyroid/parathyroid surgery and wants to apply adult FPD cutoffs to children. What is the best response?

options.text: Apply adult criteria because anatomy is identical
Use age-specific pediatric evidence and guidelines; the ACTPS FPD blueprint is explicitly adult
Use no guideline because children are rare
Assume pediatric thyroid disease is always medullary

practiceQuestions.rationale: The FPD is explicitly for adult complex disease; pediatric thyroid nodule/cancer guidance is separate. Adult criteria should not be silently transferred.

title: Facial Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery Fellowship

topicGaps: Observed unique free external lecture time is 6.69 h against the 36-hour target; the remaining verified-hours gap is 29.31 h. The target-minutes in originalClipPlan and scripted episodes are not rendered media and do not reduce this gap.

Facial-nerve paralysis/reanimation still has the largest share of verified specialist lecture time. The added recordings broaden rhinoplasty and facial-aging coverage but do not resolve the other topic gaps.
Rhinoplasty: the added UCLA recording expands the functional/aesthetic domain; MEE’s public page also lists rhinoplasty, but its 2017 guideline is dated and must be checked for updates.

Mohs and nasal reconstruction are supported by linked studies and a pediatric single-case report, but those are not a current comparative standard; hours of freely accessible full lectures were not verified for these domains.

Facial aging now has one broad UCTV recording, but consent, cultural sensitivity, aging-face outcomes, periocular/ear, hair, scar, microtia, trauma/global-surgery and research/ethics domains remain unevenly supported by full-length recordings.
No public weighted ABFPRS content blueprint was identified; exam format is not a blueprint. The course-designed crosswalk must not be represented as official exam categories.
No authentic facial case image was reproduced or verified for free reuse. Link-only case resources retain source-specific rights and consent limits.

medical.boardStatus: A distinct ABFPRS certification and exam exist. Current public requirements include eligible primary training/certification, two years in practice, 100 accepted operative reports, an eight-hour written/oral examination, accredited facility, appropriate licensure and its code of ethics. Exam-development page describes 300 written MCQs and oral examination of 12 cosmetic/reconstructive patient problems. No public weighted blueprint was identified; course domains are not official categories. ABFPRS is not listed in the ABMS Member Board roster checked 2026-10-07. ACGME Plastic Surgery lists Hand Surgery and Craniofacial Plastic Surgery; that page does not establish MEE fellowship status or status in another specialty. AAFPRS Foundation has a separate fellowship framework; do not equate it with ACGME accreditation or ABMS board status.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: This self-study course supplies no MD/DO, residency, ACGME/RCPSC training, fellowship appointment/certificate, operative experience/log, two years in practice, peer review, license, accredited facility, application eligibility or certification. Confirm current pathway with ABFPRS, primary board, AAFPRS, programme and regulators. Completion cannot guarantee eligibility or passing.

topicGaps: Observed unique free external lecture time is 6.69 h against the 36-hour target; the remaining verified-hours gap is 29.31 h. The target-minutes in originalClipPlan and scripted episodes are not rendered media and do not reduce this gap.

Facial-nerve paralysis/reanimation still has the largest share of verified specialist lecture time. The added recordings broaden rhinoplasty and facial-aging coverage but do not resolve the other topic gaps.
Rhinoplasty: the added UCLA recording expands the functional/aesthetic domain; MEE’s public page also lists rhinoplasty, but its 2017 guideline is dated and must be checked for updates.

Mohs and nasal reconstruction are supported by linked studies and a pediatric single-case report, but those are not a current comparative standard; hours of freely accessible full lectures were not verified for these domains.

Facial aging now has one broad UCTV recording, but consent, cultural sensitivity, aging-face outcomes, periocular/ear, hair, scar, microtia, trauma/global-surgery and research/ethics domains remain unevenly supported by full-length recordings.
No public weighted ABFPRS content blueprint was identified; exam format is not a blueprint. The course-designed crosswalk must not be represented as official exam categories.
No authentic facial case image was reproduced or verified for free reuse. Link-only case resources retain source-specific rights and consent limits.

practiceQuestions.stem: A new facial weakness is being considered for the label Bell’s palsy. What first step matches the AAO-HNSF guideline?

options.text: Order routine imaging before history.
Use history and examination to exclude identifiable causes.
Diagnose from unilateral weakness alone.
Wait three months before assessing alternatives.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline strongly recommends history and examination to exclude identifiable causes; routine imaging is not recommended in typical new-onset Bell’s palsy.

practiceQuestions.stem: For Bell’s palsy patients aged 16 or older, what does the cited guideline recommend?

options.text: Oral steroids within 72 hours of onset.
Steroids only after three months.
Antivirals alone.
No treatment in all cases.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The 2013 guideline recommends oral steroids within 72 hours for patients aged 16 and older; clinical qualifiers and updates must be checked.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional Bell’s palsy case has impaired eye closure. Which guideline action is strongly recommended?

options.text: Routine electrodiagnostics in all incomplete cases.
Eye protection.
No follow-up.
Antivirals alone.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline strongly recommends eye protection when closure is impaired.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which finding is a referral/reassessment trigger in the guideline?

options.text: Incomplete recovery at three months.
Any uncomplicated case at 24 hours.
Complete recovery with no symptoms.
Normal examination.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Triggers include new or worsening neurologic findings, ocular symptoms, and incomplete recovery at three months.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional facial weakness evolves over weeks and affects only one region. What is the defensible inference?

options.text: Automatically typical Bell’s palsy.
Atypical features merit evaluation for another cause.
Imaging is never appropriate regardless of findings.
This proves malignancy.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline emphasizes exclusion of identifiable causes; the vignette alone establishes no diagnosis.

practiceQuestions.stem: A 2024 meta-analysis compares nerve reconstruction techniques. What is the careful interpretation?

options.text: One method is proven best for everyone.
No statistically significant pooled difference was detected; heterogeneous evidence does not prove equivalence.
Surgery is always ineffective.
It establishes an ABFPRS blueprint.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The review reports p=0.1611 for differences among approaches and notes limited/heterogeneous studies; this cannot establish equivalence or a universal choice.

practiceQuestions.stem: The MEE page overview says one or two years, while its curriculum calls it a one-year experience. What should a course report do?

options.text: Choose two years as fact.
Report the page discrepancy and seek programme confirmation.
Infer ACGME accreditation.
Promise a research year.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The primary page contains both statements. Preserve them; do not infer current schedule or accreditation.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which requirements appear on the ABFPRS initial-certification page?

options.text: Completion of this online course alone.
Prior eligible specialty training/certification, two practice years, 100 accepted operative reports and an eight-hour written/oral exam among other requirements.
One unproctored quiz.
Any fellowship guarantees certification.

practiceQuestions.rationale: These requirements are listed alongside accredited facility and appropriate licensure.

practiceQuestions.stem: How should learners use the published pediatric nasal avulsion report?

options.text: Universal standard for all children.
One authentic case to generate questions, not generalize; no figure copying.
Copy patient photos because the article is open.
Assume all defects follow the same plan.

practiceQuestions.rationale: It is a single case report, reports guardian consent for potentially identifiable images and is CC BY; link to it, do not rehost figures.

practiceQuestions.stem: A public lecture includes operative images. What is the proper reuse assumption?

options.text: Public availability allows download/reuse.
Link to the source; do not copy without permission or a clear license.
Physician content is public domain.
Removing identifiers automatically authorizes reuse.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Free viewing is distinct from copyright permission and consent.
